source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the bustling emergency ward, under the watchful eyes of several monitors, a nurse named Elora swiftly moved beside a gurney. The triage station was a flurry of activity, with patients seated anxiously in chairs awaiting their turn. Whispers of concern floated through the air, punctuated by urgent intercom messages and the rustling of papers. A patient, clutching at his chest, leaned heavily against his companion, who nervously glanced around. "This wait is unbearable," he murmured, frustration lacing his words. Across the room, Dr. Lin examined a chart near a curtained area, his movements calm yet focused. Elora approached them, clipboard in hand, ready to assess the patient's condition further. As she did so, another intercom call interrupted her, directing her to a different bay where another urgent case awaited. With a swift nod, she prepared to leave, but not before ensuring the patient's details were meticulously recorded. The air hummed with the quiet intensity of impending care, each moment marked by the relentless ticking of time. Meanwhile, Elora's colleague, Nurse Maris, administered fluids to another patient, her hands steady despite the chaos around her. The sound of footsteps mingled with the occasional beep of medical equipment, painting a picture of organized urgency. Dr. Lin stepped aside, allowing the patient to be wheeled away for further treatment. A sense of relief washed over those waiting, if only momentarily. However, another intercom announcement brought renewed tension, signaling the arrival of yet another critical case. Each step, each word, each moment, was crucial in the relentless dance of life and care within the walls of the emergency room. Elora turned towards the new call, her eyes reflecting both determination and empathy, ready to face whatever challenges lay ahead.

Beside the entrance, a screen displayed a constant stream of updates, its flashing alerts a stark reminder of the day's ongoing drama. Patients shifted uncomfortably in their seats, some lost in thought, others engaged in quiet conversation, forming alliances against the shared ordeal of waiting.

As the evening began to draw in, shadows lengthened across the room, casting deeper hues over the scene. Yet, amidst the din of alarms and murmured conversations, there persisted a quiet strength, a collective resolve that transcended the mundane details of the day-to-day operations.
